items.title: Sutro Baths ruins at sunset
items.note: Concrete bones of a Victorian swimming palace, half-flooded, right where the land quits. Climb down into the ruins and stay for the light.
items.tip: Check the tide chart — low tide opens the cave at the north end.

items.title: Morning bun at Tartine
items.note: Orange-sugar, laminated, faintly burnt at the edges. The line is the toll and it is worth paying exactly once a week.
items.tip: Get there before 9 or the morning buns are gone and you are eating a scone.

items.title: Counter seat at Swan Oyster Depot
items.note: Eighteen stools, no tables, a crab back and a cold beer at three in the afternoon. Family-run since 1912 and entirely uninterested in changing.
items.tip: Go at 2pm on a weekday. Cash is smoother than card.

items.title: The Dolores Park slope on a clear day
items.note: The whole city arranged on a hillside with the skyline in front of it. Bring a blanket, buy something from whoever walks by.
items.tip: Upper slope for sun, lower field for shade. The fog decides your evening around 5.

items.title: Ferry Plaza farmers market on a Saturday
items.note: Porchetta sandwich from Roli Roti, peaches in season, oysters if you are feeling expensive. Eat on the pier facing the bay.
items.tip: Before 9 or accept the crowds. The porchetta line moves faster than it looks.

items.title: A drink at Trick Dog
items.note: The menu is redesigned every six months around some ridiculous premise — a zodiac chart, a Pantone book — and the drinks are genuinely good underneath the bit.
items.tip: Upstairs if you can get it. Ask what the current menu is built around.

items.title: Hang gliders at Fort Funston
items.note: A cliff, a permanent onshore wind, gliders launching a few feet over your head, and more dogs than people. Strange and completely free.
items.tip: Windy even in September — bring a layer. The sand ladder down to the beach is steep.

items.title: The bison paddock in Golden Gate Park
items.note: There is a herd of American bison in the middle of the park and nobody believes you until they are standing in front of it.
items.tip: Bike it — JFK Drive is car-free. Keep going west to the windmill and Ocean Beach.

items.title: Mai tai at Li Po Lounge
items.note: A cave of red lanterns behind a stone arch, and a mai tai made from a secret Chinese liquor that will end your night on its own terms.
items.tip: One is enough. Genuinely.

items.title: Dim sum from Good Mong Kok
items.note: A bakery counter, a paper bag, eight dollars, and the best shu mai in the city. There is nowhere to sit and that is fine.
items.tip: Cash only. Point at things. Eat it on a bench in Portsmouth Square.

items.title: Cinnamon toast at Trouble Coffee
items.note: A thick slab of grilled cinnamon toast, a coconut with a straw in it, a bench facing the fog. The original and still correct.
items.tip: Walk the two blocks to Ocean Beach with it.

items.title: Riding the Powell-Hyde cable car
items.note: Touristy, expensive per minute, and still the best thing on rails in America if you stand on the running board going down Hyde.
items.tip: Board at a mid-route stop instead of the turnaround and skip the hour-long line.

items.title: Floor 7 at SFMOMA
items.note: Skip the lower floors and go straight up. Media arts, the Agnes Martin room, and a terrace with a living wall that nobody is ever on.
items.tip: Do two floors, not seven. Your feet will file a complaint otherwise.

items.title: Walking the Lands End Coastal Trail
items.note: Cypress tunnels, shipwrecks at low tide, and the bridge appearing through the trees about two thirds of the way along.
items.tip: Start at the visitor center and walk east; the labyrinth is worth the detour.

items.title: Brooklyn Bridge at dawn
items.note: Start on the Manhattan side at six. The bridge is nearly empty, the skyline lights up behind you, and you are in Dumbo for breakfast before the city wakes.
items.tip: Enter at the Centre St stairs. Stay left; the right lane is bikes and they are not joking.

items.title: Lox on a plain bagel at Russ & Daughters
items.note: A hundred-year-old appetizing shop where they slice the Gaspé so thin it goes translucent. Take a number and watch the counter work.
items.tip: Plain bagel. Do not argue with this. Sable if you are feeling brave.

items.title: The Met roof garden
items.note: One commissioned sculpture a year, a bar nobody needs, and Central Park going gold underneath you while the museum quietly empties out.
items.tip: Go straight up when you arrive, then work down. Closed in winter.

items.title: A plain slice at Joe's
items.note: Folded, eaten standing at the counter, done in four minutes. The control group against which every other slice is measured.
items.tip: Plain. Standing. Do not sit down and do not get pepperoni.

items.title: First set at the Village Vanguard
items.note: A wedge-shaped basement with perfect sound and eighty years of ghosts in it. Coltrane recorded here. The tables are too small and it does not matter.
items.tip: Reserve ahead, arrive 45 minutes early for a decent seat. Cash bar.

items.title: Staten Island Ferry at sunset
items.note: Free, twenty-five minutes each way, and the best view of the harbor and the statue that exists. Ride out, turn around, ride back.
items.tip: Right side going out, left side coming back. Stand at the rail on the open deck.

items.title: Late show at the Comedy Cellar
items.note: A low brick basement where famous people drop in unannounced to work out material on eighty strangers. The 11:30 is the one worth booking.
items.tip: Two-drink minimum, and dinner upstairs at the Olive Tree gets you in the door.

items.title: Getting lost in the Ramble
items.note: Thirty-six acres of deliberately confusing woodland in the middle of the park. No sightlines, no crowds, actual birds.
items.tip: Come out at Bethesda Terrace and sit under the arcade.

items.title: Adobada from Los Tacos No. 1
items.note: Standing at a counter inside Chelsea Market eating three tacos off a tray with the right amount of pineapple on them.
items.tip: Adobada, then one al pastor. Handmade tortilla is worth the upcharge.

items.title: The Roosevelt Island tram
items.note: A commuter cable car that takes a subway swipe and floats you over the East River past the Queensboro Bridge at rooftop height.
items.tip: Costs a normal fare. Ride it both ways at dusk and stand at the front.

items.title: The third floor of the Strand
items.note: Eighteen miles of books, and the rare book room upstairs is a quiet wood-panelled break from the scrum downstairs.
items.tip: Start on three and work down. Buy one book. One.

items.title: Sitting on the Domino Park steps
items.note: Salvaged syrup tanks, a stretch of waterfront, and the Manhattan skyline doing the thing it does. Tacos from the stand behind you.
items.tip: Walk north to the ferry landing and take the boat back instead of the L.

items.title: Cumin lamb noodles at Xi'an Famous Foods
items.note: Hand-ripped noodles, enough cumin to change your personality, and a bill under fifteen dollars. Ten minutes start to finish.
items.tip: Spicy means spicy. The cold skin noodles on the side are the real order.

items.title: Two adjectives at Attaboy
items.note: No menu, no sign, no reservations. You say two words about what you want and someone builds it in front of you.
items.tip: Say something specific — 'bitter and a little mean' works better than 'something good'.

feed.note: Finally did the dawn walk. Nobody on the bridge. Nobody.
Waited 50 minutes for a stool. Crab back, sourdough, out in 25. Correct trade.
Surprise drop-in. Won't say who. Joe's at 1am hit different after.
Bison were asleep. Windmill was great. Would go again with a picnic.
Roof garden empty at open. Went straight up, stayed an hour.
